(3)Smt.Mahinder Kaur Partner of respondent no.2 Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
1 w/o late Harjeet Singh (4)Sh.Harshit Singh Partner of respondent no.2 s/o Harjeet Singh Both r/o E-2, Gagan Enclave Extn., Ghaziabad, U.P. ...
Respondents Date of Institution : 20.09.2014 Date of Arguments : 02.11.2023 Date of pronouncement : 16.11.2023 AWAR D 1.
This is claim petition filed u/s 166/140 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation in respect of death of Ms.Swati Singh d/o petitioner no.1 and 2 in a road side accident.
As per the petitioners accident took place on 23.05.2014 at 8.30 p.m. near Nasirpur Crossing, Ghaziabad, UP.

It is stated that on that day deceased Ms.Swati Singh was going to her home along with her colleague Sh.Ashish Srivastava on his TVS motorcycle no. UP 14CF 3468, from her office and when they reached near Nasirpur Crossing, white Accent car no.UP 14BB 6016, being driven by respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner and in a high speed, hit the above mentioned TVS motorcycle
, resultantly both the riders of the said motorcycle fell down and offending vehicle/car crushed both of them and allegedly fled away from there.
It is stated that incident was seen by one scooterist MACT No.1267/2016 Page 2 Harender Kumar who noted down registration number of offending vehicle/car.

Regarding the incidence in question FIR No.468/2014 of PS Sihani Gate was registered u/s 279/338/304A IPC.
2.

Originally the present claim petition was filed against respondent no.1 Harjeet Singh (driver) and respondent no.2, 3 and 4, out of which respondent no.2 is firm M/s M-Three Printpack (partnership firm/ owner of offending vehicle), respondent no.3 and 4 being partner in that firm.
Whereas respondent no.5 was insurance company.

Later during the investigation upon an application moved under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC by respondent no.5 insurance company, respondent no.5 was deleted from array of parties by order dated 03.02.2016 on the ground that offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 was not insured at the time of accident as said vehicle was insured with respondent no.5 on 17.06.2014 vide policy no.1302442347001228.
As such at the time of accident vehicle was found to be not insured.

3. WS has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 to 4 taking an objection that petitioners have concealed material facts and are not entitled for compensation against respondent no.1 and 2 on account of the fact that offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 was never involved in the accident.

It is stated that respondents have been implicated in present claim petition on the basis of false involvement of vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 in criminal case whereas that vehicle never caused the accident in question.

It is pleaded that police officials had come to the house of respondent no.1 to 4,
after 22- 25 days of the incidence and falsely involved the vehicle.

It is stated that at the time of alleged accident respondent no.1/driver about 63-64 years of age and was suffering from cancer from last one year prior and therefore was not in a position to drive the offending vehicle.

It was pleaded that at MACT No.1267/2016 Page 3 the time of accident the vehicle in question was not in Ghaziabad and this fact can be reflected from the mobile location of respondent no.4 Harshit Singh who along with his brother Rahul Dhingra and one Vipul Malhotra had gone in that vehicle to Gurgaon for some official work at M/s Stalwart Lifestyle.

4. Another objection is taken that court at Delhi has no jurisdiction to entertain the present claim petition as accident has taken place in UP, petitioners as well as respondents are also residents of UP.

It is pleaded that on the basis of a false and fabricated rent agreement present clam petition has Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
2 been filed.

5. On the basis of pleadings as come on the record ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 03.02.2016 framed following issues :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.UP-14BB-6016 on 23.05.2014 at 8.30 pm near Nazeer Pur Fatak at the turn of Jhankar Palace,
Ghaziabad, U.P. in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against TVS motorcycle bearing no. UP-14CF-3468
as a result its occupant namely Ms.Swati Singh fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief 6.
During the course of proceedings respondent no.1 expired.

Since the LRs of deceased respondent no.1 were already on record being respondent no.3 and 4.
7.
In order to substantiate their claim petitioner no.1 Ms.Neel Kamal has appeared as PW1, PW2 is Harender Kumar, stated to be eye witness of the incidence, PW3 is Ms.Kamlesh.
On behalf of respondents two witnesses have been examined R1W1 is Ajay Kumar, Nodal officer MACT No.1267/2016 Page 4 from Bharti Airtel and PW RW1 is respondent no.3 is Rahul Dhingra.
8. I have heard Sh.K.P. Singh, ld. Counsel for the petitioners and Sh.Sanjeev Mehta, ld. Counsel for respondents.
I have also gone through the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner as well as respondents.
Issue No.1 9.
Before I decide the question of alleged rash and negligent driving of vehicle/car bearing registration no.UP 14BB 6016, since respondent no.1 to 4 have taken two important objections.

Firstly regarding territorial jurisdiction of Delhi Tribunal to entertain the present claim petition,
secondly regarding non-involvement of vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 in the accident.
10. This Tribunal is first taking up the issue regarding territorial jurisdiction of the claim tribunal of Delhi to entertain the present claim petition.

Although an application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC moved by respondent no.1 to 4 on the ground of territorial jurisdiction was dismissed by ld.
Predecessor of this Tribunal vide order dated 07.09.2017.
Moreover no separate issue on this aspect has been framed.

Still this Tribunal finds it appropriate in view of the specific argument raised on behalf of respondent no.1 and 4 and therefore finds it appropriate to decide this aspect, in the light of evidence as come on the record.
11. As noted above admittedly accident in question has taken place in Ghaziabad UP, within the jurisdiction of PS Sihani Gate where FIR No.468/2014 was registered regarding that accident.
Admittedly respondents are also not residents of Delhi.

Earlier when claim petition was filed,
insurance company having registered office at Delhi was made respondent no.5 but as noted above respondent no.5 was deleted from the array of parties as at the time of accident the alleged vehicle was not MACT No.1267/2016 Page 5 insured and that fact was undisputed.
Another reason for filing Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/

3 the claim petition in Delhi Tribunal was a rent agreement relied upon by the petitioners to show that after the accident i.e. on 11.09.2014 a rent deed was executed between one Kamlesh (PW3) and petitioner no.1 Ms.Neel Kamal for first floor of property no. B-1/485, Gali No.17, Harsh Vihar, Delhi.
Respondents no.1 to 1 to have disputed this rent agreement and alleged it to be a fabricated document, created for making out a jurisdiction in Delhi for filing the present claim petition.
12. In this regard PW1 Ms.Neel Kamal in her evidence, inter alia referred to rent agreement as Ex.PW1/5.
In cross-examination PW1 stated that she resided in Delhi from 2013 to 2015 in above mentioned address.
PW1 admitted in cross-examination that she has no other document except the rent agreement Ex.PW1/5 to prove that she resided in Delhi during the aforesaid period.

PW1 admitted in her cross-examination that she has a permanent residential address of Ghaziabad,
Aadhar card, voter card and bank accounts at the address of Ghaziabad UP.
PW3 Ms.Kamlesh has deposed that she is the owner of above mentioned property of Harsh Vihar Delhi and real elder sister of petitioner no.1.

PW3 stated that since petitioner was having dispute with her in laws,
therefore on her request she let out the above mentioned property of Harsh Vihar to petitioner under the rent agreement Ex.PW1/5.

PW3 further proved her ownership documents as Ex.PW3/1 and Ex.PW3/2.
13.

Having considered the submissions and examining the evidence, at the outset it be noted that PW3 being owner of house no.B- 1/485, Gali No.17, Harsh Vihar, Delhi has proved the execution of rent agreement Ex.PW1/5 and has also given the reason as to why rent agreement was so executed.
In cross-examination of PW3 nothing MACT No.1267/2016 Page 6 substantive came out to disbelieve the execution of rent agreement dated 11.09.2014.
PW1 in her cross-examination also reiterated regarding rent agreement and residing in Delhi from 2013 to 2015.
It be noted that during the inquiry proceedings of a claim petition, petitioner is required to prove a particular fact only by preponderance of probability.

Assessing the evidence as come on the record this Tribunal is of considered view that nothing came on the record to establish that rent agreement Ex.PW1/5 is forged or fabricated, when the executant of the same PW3 Ms.Kamlesh has appeared in the witness box and PW1 Ms.Neel Kamal in whose favour same was executed has also proved the same.
There being nothing in their cross-examination to show that rent agreement was fabricated.

No doubt it came in the cross-examination of PW1 that she along with her husband has been residing at 341,
Daulatpura Ghaziabad and their Aadhar card, voting card and bank accounts are also of Ghaziabad address. But that fact in itself is not sufficient to conclude that at no point of time petitioners have resided at Delhi.

A rent agreement Ex.PW1/5 in the opinion of this Tribunal has been proved by preponderance of probabilities and therefore this Tribunal finds that it has jurisdiction to entertain the present claim petition.
14. Now comes the question regarding involvement of vehicle bearing registration no.UP 14BB 6016 as well as the question of rash and negligent driving.
PW1 Ms.Neel Kamal though stated about the accident but she admitted in her cross-examination that she was not the eye witness to the accident.
PW2 Harender Kumar is eye witness to the accident who stated that he is Advocate and maternal uncle of deceased.

On 23.05.2014 PW2 was going to Bhatia More from Ghaziabad District Court via Nasirpur Crossing and when he reached near Jhankar Palace, he saw offending car MACT No.1267/2016 Page 7 white colour Accent bearing registration no.UP 14BB 6016 came in a rash and Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
4 negligent manner and in a high speed and struck forcefully the motorcycle no.UP14CF 3468, being driven by Ashish Shrivastava and deceased in this case was pillion rider
. PW2 says that on account of the impact Ashish Shrivastava as well as deceased fell down and sustained multiple fractures/head fatal injuries.
PW2 says that driver of the offending car (respondent no.1) fled from the spot of accident, PW2 stated to have chased him and in that process noted down the registration number.
Thereafter he came back and was shocked to see that pillion rider of the motorcycle was his own niece (bhanji).
PW2 says that he immediately took his niece to Sudarshan Multi Specialty Hospital Ghaziabad.

PW2 stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016.
15.

PW2 was duly cross examined wherein he admitted that his statement was recorded by the police in the investigation of criminal case and his name is mentioned in the list of witnesses of charge sheet in that case.
PW2 further admitted that his name is not mentioned in the MLC of deceased prepared at Sudarshan Hospital, PW2 however stated that his name is mentioned in consent column.
PW2 further admitted that he did not inform the police after the accident but witness has explained that he removed his niece to hospital first and then police was informed from the hospital.

On reading of PW2 nothing has come in cross-examination to disbelieve the version of the witness regarding the manner of accident as well as rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending car no.UP 14BB 6016.
16.

In this context it is important to assess the contentions raised on behalf of respondent no.1 to 4 to the effect that vehicle was not at all MACT No.1267/2016 Page 8 involved in the accident and UP police, investigating FIR No.468/2014 of PS Sihani Gate, falsely involved the vehicle in question.
Whereas at the time of accident vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 was in Gurgaon.
To substantiate this fact respondent o.1 o 4 examined two witnesses.
R1W1 is Nodal officer of Bharti Airtel who proved the subscription details of mobile no.9910199005 in the name of Vipul Malhotra as well as mobile no.9717835959, in the name of Harshit Dhingra.
R1W1 further proved the CDR of above mentioned mobile numbers Ex.R1W1/D with certificate u/s 65B of Evidence Act.

This Tribunal need not to go into details as even if the CDR of above mentioned mobile phones establish their location to be in Gurgaon, that fact hardly proves the fact that two persons namely Vipul Malhotra and Harshit Dhingra whose mobile locations were in Gurgaon were driving the offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 to Gurgaon.

Mobile location of above mentioned two persons does not establish the physical location of offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016.
17.

This brings this Tribunal to examine the evidence of RW1 Rahul Dhingra who in his affidavit of examination in chief stated that on 23.05.2014 he along with his brother Harshit and one friend Vipul Malhotra had gone to Gurgaon for some official work of firm M/s Stalwork in the vehicle in question no.UP 14BB 6016 which was being driven by Harshit Dhingra.
PW RW1 though admitted that vehicle in question was impounded by UP Police but deposed that the above said vehicle has been falsely involved in the accident by UP Police.

In cross-examination recorded before LC RW1 Rahul Dhingra admitted that in respect of accident in question FIR was registered and in that FIR vehicle in question was impounded after 22-23 days of accident.
Witness further admitted that he got released the impounded vehicle on superdari from Ghaziabad court.

Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
5 MACT No.1267/2016 Page 9 PW RW1 though denied having been served with notice u/s 133 M.V.
Act, however the certified copy of notice u/s 133 M.V. Act served during the investigation of FIR No.468/2014 copy of which is on the record wherein statement of Rahul Dhingra in the notice u/s 133 M.V. Act has been recorded whereby Rahul Dhingra admitted his father late Harjeet Singh (R1)
was driving the Accent car no.UP 14BB 6016 at the time of accident. This admission on the notice which is part of criminal case record of FIR No.468/2014 coupled with the police file observation,
establish the involvement of vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 in the accident.

As such the Tribunal finds that in view of the evidence of PW1, PW2 involvement of vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 in the accident is proved and respondent no.1 to 4 have failed to disprove the same by their evidence for the reasons as noted above.

18. On the aspect of rash and negligent driving, it is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No.
550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 10 19.

sentences.text: In the facts of the present case PW3 has cogently deposed regarding the manner in which the accident has taken place and testified that vehicle bearing no.UP 14BB 6016 was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which it hit the motorcycle, on which the deceased was pillion rider.
Evidence of PW3 has been consistent and cogent as nothing came in the cross-examination to disbelieve his version.
Moreover admittedly R1 late Harjeet Singh was prosecuted in FIR No.468/2014 for the accident in question.

In the criminal record documents including report u/s 173 Cr.PC, site plan of accident and mechanical report of offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 as well as mechanical inspection report of motorcycle no.UP14CE 3468.

In this context it was argued that if the testimony of PW3 is examined regarding the manner in which accident has taken place, version regarding accident is belied by the fact that mechanical inspection report does not indicate any damage to offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016.
No doubt as per mechanical inspection report RW2/4 of offending vehicle there was no much damage noted by mechanical inspection.

However this Tribunal does not find it to be of much significance considering the fact that vehicle was impounded after about one month of the accident and therefore there is every possibility of repairing the vehicle and getting the damaged portion of the vehicle to be dented and painted.

20. Thus keeping in view the evidence of PW3 coupled with report u/s 173 Cr.PC and site plan this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on the record to prove that accident in this case has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 who was driving the offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 as it is proved by notice u/s 133 M.V. Act that on the notice itself son of R1 had Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
6 admitted that the vehicle was MACT No.1267/2016 Page 11 being driven by R1 at the time of accident.

Thus issue stands decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no.1 to 4.
Issue No.2 21.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 22.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Ms.Swati Singh.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
7 19.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 13 Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
23.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Medical Expenses 24.

To prove the expenditure incurred by petitioners towards medical bills of the deceased, it is deposed by PW1 that immediately after the accident she was taken to Sudarshan Multi Speciality Hospital where she was declared dead after some treatment.
She proved death certificate and medical treatment record/bills as Ex.PW1/3 (colly.).

Perusal of such medical bills which are duly attested by Sudarshan Hospital shows that a total sum of Rs.9,500/- has been spent by petitioners uupon Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
8 medical treatment of deceased.
Thus, this Tribunal awards compensation for a sum of Rs.9,500/- to the petitioners under this head.
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 14

Age of deceased :
25.
The petitioner (PW1) in her evidence has proved educational documents of deceased as Ex.PW1/1, her PAN card as Ex.PW1/2, voter I- card and ration card of petitioners as Ex.PW1/4.
Perusal of copy of high speed certificate Ex.PW1/1 (colly.) of deceased shows that her date of birth was 17.05.1993.
Same date of birth of deceased has been shown to be mentioned in her PAN card.
These documents in the opinion of this Tribunal are conclusive proof of age of deceased.

Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (23.05.2014)
was 21 years.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
26.
Petitioner (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased daughter was pursuing LLB Ist Year and thereafter she took admission in M.Com in the year 2014.
She deposed that at the time of accident her daughter was working as a Manager in M/s On spot Cool Point at K.M. 43, Kavi Nagar, Ghaziabad, UP and she was getting Rs.14,000/- per month as a salary.
PW1 has proved office Identity card of deceased as Ex.PW1/3 and salary certificate of deceased as Ex.PW1/6.
During cross-examination PW1 stated that her deceased daughter was getting salary in cash.
There is no dispute to the deposition of PW1 by any of the respondents as no evidence in rebuttal has been brought with regard to income of the deceased.
Thus the testimony of PW1 remain unrebutted and unchallenged.
27. Identity card Ex.PW1/2 of deceased shows that she was working as Manager in M/s On Spot Air Conditioning and date of issue of such Identity card is 01.01.2013.
Salary certificate Ex.PW1/6 dated 18.06.2014 of the deceased for the month of shows that she was getting salary of Rs.14,000/- per month.
Contrary evidence in contrary has come MACT No.1267/2016 Page 15 on record.
Therefore as per evidence and documents placed on record income of deceased is assessed to be Rs.14,000/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
28.
As held above, deceased was 21 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:
 MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
9  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above 29.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against the age bracket of 21 to 25 years to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
30.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 16 "(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

31. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged 21 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
32.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards her personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 17  Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
10  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
33.

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by three petitioners i.e. parents and brother of deceased.
Petitioner no.2 father of deceased must be earning to support his family, therefore he cannot be said to be dependent upon the deceased.
Petitioner no.3 is brother of the deceased and since his parents including father are alive, he also cannot be said to be dependent upon the deceased.
Therefore one-half of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
34.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.44,000/-,
16,500/- and Rs.16,500/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses
is required to be granted.

Further, in MACT No.1267/2016 Page 18 view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is claim petition filed u/s 166/140 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation in respect of death of Ms.Swati Singh d/o petitioner no.1 and 2 in a road side accident.
Later during the investigation upon an application moved under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC by respondent no.5 insurance company, respondent no.5 was deleted from array of parties by order dated 03.02.2016 on the ground that offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016 was not insured at the time of accident as said vehicle was insured with respondent no.5 on 17.06.2014 vide policy no.1302442347001228.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of pleadings as come on the record ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 03.02.2016 framed following issues :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.UP-14BB-6016 on 23.05.2014 at 8.30 pm near Nazeer Pur Fatak at the turn of Jhankar Palace,
Ghaziabad, U.P. in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against TVS motorcycle bearing no. UP-14CF-3468
as a result its occupant namely Ms.Swati Singh fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It be noted that during the inquiry proceedings of a claim petition, petitioner is required to prove a particular fact only by preponderance of probability.
A rent agreement Ex.PW1/5 in the opinion of this Tribunal has been proved by preponderance of probabilities and therefore this Tribunal finds that it has jurisdiction to entertain the present claim petition.
Mobile location of above mentioned two persons does not establish the physical location of offending vehicle no.UP 14BB 6016.
17.
18. On the aspect of rash and negligent driving, it is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No.
550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation &
Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 10 19.
In the facts of the present case PW3 has cogently deposed regarding the manner in which the accident has taken place and testified that vehicle bearing no.UP 14BB 6016 was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which it hit the motorcycle, on which the deceased was pillion rider.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 22.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death:
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and MACT No.1267/2016 Page 12 (c) the number of dependents.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
31. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged 21 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
32.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards her personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
MACT No.1267/2016 Page 17  Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd Neelkamal vs Harjeet Singh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32633102/
10  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)

Petitioner no.2 father of deceased must be earning to support his family, therefore he cannot be said to be dependent upon the deceased.
Petitioner no.3 is brother of the deceased and since his parents including father are alive, he also cannot be said to be dependent upon the deceased.
